title: Swing a car's sun visor off its clip to the side window and slide it out to shade the glass
instruction: Move the sun visor over to shade the side window, covering the marked band on the glass.
context: Swinging the visor off its centre clip beneath the car's headliner to block low sun through the side window is something nearly every driver does; it requires pulling the rod out of a sprung clip, swinging the visor 90 degrees beneath the roof header, and sliding the blade out along its rod. Closest accepted look-alikes: TK-VGVBNZ (a casement window's peg stay) and TK-T5MAQE (a car headrest); here one part must be pulled out of a sprung clip, swung 90 degrees under the roof header and slid along its rod, three motions on three axes in a cramped overhead space.
setup: A self-supporting benchtop mock-up of a car's driver-side front roof corner stands on the station table (turned 180 deg around Z with pivot origin at world x = 0.34 m, y = +0.22 m, rod height 330 mm above the bench, reproducible either with a 2013-2017 Honda Accord EX left sliding sun visor 83280-T2F-A52ZB / 83280-T2F-A52ZA, ~USD 35 aftermarket / ~USD 104 used OEM / ~USD 308 new dealer OEM, and matching Accord retainer clip 88217-TR0-A01ZL / 88217-TR0-A01ZA, ~USD 10, or with the six exact-frame 1:1 printable STLs from generate_cad_stl.py (off-centre 75 mm rod-bore blade halves joined by M3 dowels plus M3-pinned clevis clip with a 90 deg torsion spring) on an 8 mm steel L-rod and 2020 extrusion frame). Three 30 x 30 mm structural posts stand on the bench (front A-pillar at frame (-0.065, -0.145) m, rear B-pillar at (-0.650, -0.145) m, and right header stanchion at (-0.125, +0.515) m) supporting: (1) an overhead windshield header and stowed-visor roof/headliner canopy (176 mm deep x 690 mm wide, frame x in [-0.156, +0.020] m, y in [-0.160, +0.530] m, molded cloth headliner ceiling 44 to 56 mm above the rod plus 8 mm painted steel roof skin, with two 56 x 72 x 16 mm mounting bosses at +28 to +44 mm enveloping the outer pivot bezel and centre clip and an 8 x 20 mm black EPDM rubber pinch-weld guard along the front lip); (2) a 509 x 90 mm driver-side roof cantrail and headliner valence (frame x in [-0.665, -0.156] m, y in [-0.155, -0.065] m) above a 590 x 30 x 40 mm upper door header; and (3) a shatter-safe 570 x 272 x 4 mm clear polycarbonate side window pane at frame y = -0.120 m (from 18 mm above the bench to 40 mm below the rod) with all four edges encased in continuous 14 x 14 mm black EPDM rubber U-channel weatherstrip molding (zero exposed edges) and a 300 x 120 mm orange tape target band at frame x in [-0.550, -0.250] m, z in [-0.165, -0.045] m. Bolted into the headliner bosses 330 mm above the bench are the sun visor (430 x 170 x 25 mm padded blade centered 75 mm off its 8 mm steel L-rod of length 462 mm, 0.35 kg: outer Z swivel 0 to 88 deg, rod Y roll -100 to 0 deg, and axial Y slide 0 to 120 mm, each holding by friction) and the centre retainer clip at y = +0.454 m (fixed front jaw and torsion-sprung rear jaw). The visor starts hanging straight down (-90 deg roll), retracted (0 mm slide), with its rod tip clipped in the centre clip.
scoring: End state only. 0 unless all six independent hand points (both jaw pad tips and the independent gripper pad-center datum on each arm) are at least 80 mm from every part (including the roof, headliner, pillars, weatherstrip, clip, and visor) and no surface point on any part moved 1 mm or more across the final 1.0 s (21 samples at 20 Hz; checked in real trials by tape measure and 1.0 s video stillness). Then the visor's outline projected square-on onto the side window from inside (checked in real trials by a straight-on photo normal to the window or ruler against the orange tape border) is compared with the 300 x 120 mm marked band: 1.0 if it covers at least 80% of the band's area, 0.5 if at least 40%, and 0.0 otherwise. Swung over without sliding out it covers ~61% (0.5); slid out >=50 mm it covers >=80% (1.0). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the visor blade fully forward along its rod to its 0 mm stop, swing the visor back across beneath the headliner, and press the rod tip into the sprung centre clip with the blade hanging straight down (-90 deg). Inspect the EPDM rubber edge-trim channels on the window and header before each trial.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz with overhead roof/headliner canopy, side cantrail, and 4-edge EPDM weatherstrip matching a 2013-2017 Honda Accord EX slide-on-rod visor (83280-T2F-A52ZB + clip 88217-TR0-A01ZL) or 1:1 printable STLs (generate_cad_stl.py) at 330 mm rod height. Joint frictions (0.6 N m swivel/roll, 4 N slide), clip jaw spring (0.05 N m/rad), and rigid 430x170x25 mm blade mass (0.35 kg) are engineering estimates.
